claims.text: Standard additive manufacturing of high-entropy-alloy components typically produces significant residual stresses.
Standard additive manufacturing of high-entropy-alloy components typically produces dimensional distortions.
Standard additive manufacturing of high-entropy-alloy components typically produces microcracks.
Preheating the build platform will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to an unheated platform.
Preheating the build platform will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to an unheated platform.
Preheating the build platform will reduce fabrication-induced defects relative to an unheated platform.
Build-platform preheating reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients during solidification lower residual stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a more uniform microstructure.
Lower residual stress reduces microcrack formation.
Build-platform preheating will enhance tensile strength relative to the standard process.
Build-platform preheating will enhance ductility relative to the standard process.
The magnitude of improvement from platform preheating depends on alloy composition and processing environment.

contradictions.description: The intervention and experiment require use of an 'optimized temperature,' but the uncertainty field states that the precise optimal platform temperature has not been established; no procedure for selecting it is provided.

The boundary excludes conditions in which elevated temperature causes oxidation, whereas the falsification rule treats observed oxidation as falsifying the hypothesis rather than as placing the experiment outside its stated scope.
